column1: # Every audited instruction in Towntopia's jar: WorkSitesAuditTest fails when one listed here is missing from the jar, a
# count changed, or the jar has one not listed here.
# Columns: key<TAB>occurrences<TAB>verdict<TAB>bridge<TAB>note. key = owner#method#KIND (owner relative to com/alex/test/).
# KIND, read or call (every one in the jar is a row): RECIPES = CookActivity.RECIPES, DISHES = CookActivity.DISHES,
# INGREDIENTS = CookActivity.INGREDIENTS, RAW_FOR_COOK = CookActivity.RAW_FOR_COOK, COOK_SCHEMA = CookSettingsSchema.SCHEMA,
# SCHEMA_DISHES = CookSettingsSchema.DISHES; SHIELD, SHEARS, BUCKET, TEMPLATE_COPY = BlacksmithActivity's stock recipes;
# MAT_ITEM / MAT_ITEMS = BlacksmithActivity$Mat.item / .items; MAT_VALUES = Mat.$values() in Mat's static init;
# MAX_TIER = BlacksmithBalance.maxTier(int); RECIPE_TIER = BlacksmithActivity$Recipe.tier(); TIER_OF = ForgeOrderBook.tierOf
# calls; PLANNER_MAX_TIER / PLANNER_ORDER_TIER = reads of Planner.maxTier / .orderTier.
# Scoped KIND (only in methods rows name): INT_1..INT_5 = iconst_1..5, one row per occurrence (KIND@n, n-th in the
# method, from 1; every occurrence of a kind the method's rows name is listed; a KEEP row without @n covers every occurrence
# of the kind in the method); IRETURN / ARETURN = every return. In the smith's classes (ForgeOrderBook, $Stock,
# BlacksmithBalance, BlacksmithActivity, $Planner, $Offline, $Offline$Payment) every method's iconst_1..5 are listed:
# a tier can enter or leave only through the audited carriers, and each constant was read in context.
# occurrences: how often that kind occurs in the method in the 0.1.3 jar; a method whose count differs stays as shipped.
# Verdicts: REWRITE (the instruction goes through the bridge; bridges answer Towntopia's own value while nothing is
# registered), KEEP (Towntopia's instruction stays; listed so the audit sees every place the value flows).
# How a REWRITE row reaches its bridge depends on the kind (WorkSite.Style): reads and constants get invokestatic
# bridge(T)T after them (stock recipes: bridge(Object)Object + checkcast); Mat.item/items get dup before and
# bridge(Object mat, T)T after; maxTier gets dup before and bridge(int level, int tier)int after; returns get
# every argument loaded again + bridge(R, args...)R before them; MAT_VALUES adds townkit$extend to Mat (16 spare constants).
# bridge: internal/class/Name#method for REWRITE rows, - for KEEP.
# The smith's tier ladder (ForgeBridges onTier/onTop/onSize/onNoTable/onMaxTier/onTierOf/onRecipeTier) is used only
# while every one of its REWRITE rows was rewritten in every smith class (ForgeHooks.reach); else addon tiers,
# materials and recipe changes stay off for Towntopia's smith (one log line).
# Owners of REWRITE rows with no hooks become carrier targets (hookgen --sites), so the mixin plugin sees them.
# Smelting (0.7.1): SPARE_ORE = BlacksmithActivity.SPARE_ORE (the away catch-up's raws and ingots, read by Offline only);
# COUNT_ITEM = BlacksmithActivity.countItem(ctx, item) calls; ITEM_RAW_COPPER / ITEM_IRON_INGOT / ITEM_GOLD_INGOT /
# ITEM_COPPER_INGOT = reads of those Items fields. The last five are everywhere in the jar, so (like constants) they are
# audited only in the methods rows name, one row per occurrence (KIND@n). Style: DUP2_ARGS (COUNT_ITEM) = dup2 before the
# call, bridge(ctx, item, result) after it; returns take every argument: bridge(result, args...) (references as Object).
# In the village the smith hard-codes raw iron, gold and copper: addon raws ride its raw-copper path (SmeltBridges).
# Mining (0.7.1): SET_IS_EMPTY = Set.isEmpty() (scoped: audited only in the methods rows name, one row per occurrence); the
# miner's ore check and mine sort are the only miner reads that are rewritten (MineBridges): the lucky rolls, the druid's
# regrown rock, the settings registry and the mine fit are hooks (MineHooks). Towntopia's OreHeights, OreBlocks and Ore enum are untouched.
# Tag ingredients: INPUTS = CookActivity$Recipe.inputsPerBatch() calls (every one in the jar is a row). Style
# DUP_RECEIVER: dup before the call, bridge(Object recipe, Map inputs)Map after it. A tag dish has one Recipe whose inputs
# are its first variant; inside a cook's tick or an away cook's day the bridge answers the village's chosen variant.
